questions.prompt: A teammate marks a lesson complete when it is opened. The requested rule is “complete after every slide is reviewed.” What should you do first?
options: Specify and check the actual completion contract
Change the button color only
Assume opening and reviewing mean the same thing
questions.explanation: Resolve the precise requirement before judging or changing its implementation.

questions.prompt: Your cleanup deletes a no-match return because null looks clearer. The callers distinguish null and undefined. How should you classify the edit?
options: A formatting-only change
A behavior change that needs a separate decision and checks
Automatically safe because it is shorter
questions.explanation: Changing an observable result is not behavior-preserving refactoring.

questions.prompt: Two helpers share syntax but implement different domain policies. What is the best next step?
options: Merge them immediately to remove lines
Delete one policy
Explain their meanings and change patterns before choosing an abstraction
questions.explanation: An abstraction should express a shared idea, not conceal different requirements behind similar syntax.

questions.prompt: A bug fix includes a safe rename of a misleading flag and focused checks. Which source idea does this best apply?
options: The grand redesign race
The Boy Scout Rule
Replacing practice with reading
questions.explanation: A bounded improvement leaves the code a little easier to maintain.

questions.prompt: An apparently simple function silently reads global state. Which clean-code concern remains?
options: Its hidden dependency makes behavior and changes harder to reason about
Its font choice is incorrect
It must be replaced with the largest framework
questions.explanation: Thomas emphasizes explicit dependencies and changeability, beyond readability alone.

questions.prompt: A product’s releases slow after copied rules diverge. Which account best fits the source’s maintenance argument?
options: More copying necessarily increases speed
All delays are caused by the programming language
Tangles increase understanding and regression costs, creating pressure for further shortcuts
questions.explanation: The source describes an accumulating cycle, not a numeric law about every project.

questions.prompt: A new team promises a rewrite, but the old app keeps gaining features. What must the plan account for?
options: Matching current behavior and keeping up with a moving target
Assuming all legacy behavior is irrelevant
The impossibility of messy new code
questions.explanation: A replacement race requires parity plus ongoing changes; new code can also accumulate disorder.

questions.prompt: An unfamiliar convention differs from the book but communicates intent and fits the team. What is an appropriate response?
options: Reject it solely because another school uses a different convention
Evaluate reader benefit, behavior and consistency in context
Ignore the team’s agreed practices
questions.explanation: The Schools of Thought passage acknowledges professional alternatives and encourages broadening judgment.

questions.prompt: A reader can predict a lookup from its name and its documented contract. Which perspective does this especially illustrate?
options: Cunningham’s expectation criterion
A guarantee of zero defects
The need for hidden side effects
questions.explanation: Cunningham values routines that behave as a reader expects; this does not guarantee correctness.

questions.prompt: A developer says “We can skip tests because the code is elegant.” Which response best reflects Thomas and Jeffries?
options: Agree whenever there are fewer lines
Only names matter
Checks support safe enhancement, and passing tests comes first in the simple-code priority order
questions.explanation: Both perspectives include tests; elegance alone does not establish safe changeability.

questions.prompt: The contents name Concurrency and JUnit Internals. What can this course honestly claim?
options: It contains those full chapters
It preserves their contents/index references; their chapter text is absent
It reconstructed the author’s missing listings
questions.explanation: Full coverage is of the supplied 67 pages, not unavailable chapters in the complete book.

questions.prompt: Which final artifact best demonstrates practice rather than recall alone?
options: A copied definition with no application
A slide completion count
An explained contract, a small diff and behavior checks from your own project
questions.explanation: The introduction and conclusion emphasize applying decisions and learning through work.
